**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-admit the changed cycle-2 acceptance rule**

The admitted protocol in `runs/20260927T192740433960Z-glm-PHYS-001/round.json:9` freezes seeds 1–8/11–20 and `mean ± 4·std`, explicitly forbidding threshold changes after Stage B, but this code was added after cycle 1 failed and substitutes seeds 21–28/31–40 plus a `0.01` floor without a new admitted round. Consequently, the reported cycle-2 PASS is post-hoc rather than the claimed pre-registered confirmation; start and admit a new round containing this rule before using its result.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the frozen B3 energy criterion**

For every cycle-2 Stage B sample, this loop checks only the structure-function and spectrum bands; it neither constructs an energy threshold nor compares `m["energy_rel_residual"]`. The frozen acceptance contract at `runs/20260927T192740433960Z-glm-PHYS-001/round.json:9` requires B3 (`energy residual <= 2× Stage A maximum`), while the report claims the energy residuals passed, so `CALIBRATED_BASELINE_PASS` can be emitted without establishing that required conservation check.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/e22a993feb072ec8a575c44ed0f9328571b4e2bb/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Running the newly supplied `verify_manifest.py` at this exact commit reports mismatches for 7 of the 9 manifest entries, including this first script hash, both result JSON files, both band files, the baseline script, and the amplitude guard. Thus the committed evidence fails its own integrity verifier before any reproduction attempt and cannot authenticate the reported results; regenerate the manifest from the final committed artifacts.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/e22a993feb072ec8a575c44ed0f9328571b4e2bb/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

When W3 is evaluated, the final lags 152 and 156 nearly duplicate one endpoint while the preceding values follow an approximately 1.25 ratio, so this is not the admitted “13 geometric points” specified in `round.json:9`. The extra endpoint weight changes every reported W3 slope, window-sensitivity statistic, and W3 separation check relative to the frozen design; use a genuinely geometric 13-point grid or re-admit this exact list before reporting those results.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L8-L8](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/81c7c3723b98615c44990a58f438401bfb2dfcae/AGENTS.md#L8-L8)

For the cycle-2 PASS, this output retains only row counts and up to ten violations; because the violation list is empty, none of the 72 calibration or 90 confirmation measurements—including the raw B3 energy residuals—are preserved. This prevents an independent audit of the claimed 0/90 result or numerical-error behavior without rerunning the experiment and violates `VALIDATION.md:7`'s raw-residual requirement; save the Stage A/B rows with beta, seed, and window metadata in the result or a hashed raw artifact.

The purported frozen `bands2.json` rounds every SF and spectrum boundary to four decimals, while Stage B evaluates the unrounded in-memory `bands` values on lines 75–82. A measurement within roughly 5e-5 of a boundary can therefore receive a different verdict when checked against the committed frozen artifact, so the artifact is not the acceptance contract actually used; serialize the full-precision bounds and use those persisted values for Stage B.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the runtime that produced the r2 evidence**

This environment artifact records only the governance pin, base, and branch, omitting the Python version and platform even though the cycle-1 verdict depends on last-bit floating-point behavior: replaying this exact commit under Python 3.14.4 produced 0 violations and `CALIBRATED_BASELINE_PASS`, while the committed result reports 3 violations and `CALIBRATED_BASELINE_FAIL` against bands only about 1e-14 wide. Without the producer runtime, the failure that motivates cycle 2 cannot be reproduced; record at least the interpreter and platform used for r2.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/7219b6ab57ada9e324ddf1d508ea1d13e931f84c/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the frozen B3 energy bound**

The cycle-1 acceptance contract in `round.json` fixes B3 at no more than twice the Stage A maximum, but this applies a `1e-10` floor; with the committed Stage A residuals around `1e-14`, that relaxes the limit by roughly three orders of magnitude and can report an energy pass that the admitted rule rejects. Unlike the previously flagged cycle-2 omission, this defect remains in the cycle-1 evaluator; remove the floor or formally admit it before execution.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L8-L8](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/88c316ce666af63c7e6b9eedbb975e3dbf6dc20e/AGENTS.md#L8-L8)

Fresh evidence after the commands-list remediation is that this entry is still descriptive prose rather than a valid invocation: `python (inline: ...)` cannot be executed, and a repo-wide search finds no checked-in generator for `amplitude_guard_check.json`. A verifier therefore cannot regenerate that evidence; record the actual heredoc/`python -c` invocation or add a script and reference it here.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/88c316ce666af63c7e6b9eedbb975e3dbf6dc20e/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare matching physical lag windows across N**

For the implemented field `cos(2πkj/N)`, a lag index `r` represents the normalized separation `r/N`; reusing the same integer `WINDOWS` for `N=2048` and `N=4096` therefore halves every physical fitting interval. Consequently, the reported `m4096 - m2048` values conflate resolution sensitivity with a factor-of-two window shift and cannot support the claimed N-sensitivity analysis. Scale the lag indices with N (or otherwise hold the physical interval fixed) before comparing the slopes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the UV cutoff before rejecting the β=3 window**

The logarithmic formula also requires `k_hi*r >> 1`, but in the claimed regime `r < 0.0248` one instead has `k_hi*r < 0.035`, where the finite sum is in its analytic UV `r²` regime. Calling the script's exact `local_exponent` gives 1.974 at `r=1` and 1.912 at `r=2`, while an OLS fit over integer lags `[1,4]` gives 1.906, directly contradicting the statement that no `r >= 1` reaches 1.9. The audit should distinguish this cutoff-induced `r²` behavior from marginal inertial-range scaling rather than applying the continuum approximation outside its validity domain.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/537561c42f168e8d3426d3c6a8e13ea9d3c0496e/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report the numerical method that was actually executed**

This says the value was computed with `mpmath` at 40 digits, but the committed script imports no `mpmath`, performs ordinary double-precision Simpson integration, and ignores its `--dps` argument. Because this document is the canonical evidence record, the current wording falsely attributes the result to a calculation that was not run; either execute and preserve that multiprecision check or describe the standard-library computation consistently here.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/537561c42f168e8d3426d3c6a8e13ea9d3c0496e/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

This note says hashes identify the regenerated outputs, but this `round.json` contains no data or result hashes for either committed evidence JSON or the baseline result. Deferring hash automation does not supply the required static provenance: without the values, the canonical artifacts cannot be bound to the recorded run, so the hashes should be recorded here or the regeneration claim should not be made.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/537561c42f168e8d3426d3c6a8e13ea9d3c0496e/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the reversed UV/IR cutoff logic**

Fresh evidence after `7321f2a` shows that the replacement explanation still reverses both conditions: at `r = 15`, `k_hi·r = 20.7` and `k_lo·r = 0.069`, so the window satisfies the document's own UV/IR gates rather than violating the UV condition, while `r < 0.025` satisfies the IR condition but fails the UV one. Consequently, the claim that the marginal regime is squeezed out entirely does not follow; moreover, `s2_local_exponent.py` and its generated JSON still retain the explicitly disproven statement that no `r >= 1` reaches 1.9. The cutoff interpretation and generated evidence need to be corrected consistently.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/7321f2af077cb832786ea87b7aec4233885baccd/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record failure of the frozen high-precision criterion**

The frozen B4 criterion above requires a high-precision evaluation plus the sweep, but the committed implementation explicitly performs ordinary double-precision Simpson integration, ignores `--dps`, and the audit acknowledges that no multiprecision check is reproduced by a committed command. Marking `all_criteria_passed` true therefore silently relaxes the frozen criterion after execution; either preserve and run a reproducible high-precision check or record B4 as failed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L8-L8](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/7321f2af077cb832786ea87b7aec4233885baccd/AGENTS.md#L8-L8)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the committed baseline result to the artifact manifest**

Fresh evidence after `7321f2a` is that the seven new entries still omit `problems/PHYS-001/experiments/results/r1/k41_baseline_results.json`. That committed file is produced by the reference execution and supplies the values used for the decisive comparison, so omitting its hash leaves a result artifact unbound to this round despite the new provenance claim.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/7321f2af077cb832786ea87b7aec4233885baccd/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply both cutoffs in the companion audit**

Fresh evidence after `e3c93de` is that the companion audit still applies the marginal formula without its UV condition and says the `>1.9` regime is unreachable merely because `r < 0.0248` lies below the lattice spacing. For this band, that range has `k_hi·r ≪ 1`, so the marginal formula is invalid and the exact exponent instead exceeds 1.9 at integer lags 1 and 2 because of the analytic `r²` regime; meanwhile the actual marginal window is `[15,21]` with exponent ≈1.72. This leaves the two canonical reports with contradictory cutoff interpretations, so this paragraph needs the same UV/IR correction as `CANONICAL_FACTS.md`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/e3c93deb54384c93e039cd3330602d0a0d08c604/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

If the pre-existing result cannot be removed—for example, a read-only result on Windows—this exception is silently ignored. If the subsequent reference process exits before replacing the file, the old JSON still exists, lines 213–217 load it, and the run is marked `results_fresh`, allowing stale data to support the reproduction verdict. Return an unusable result when deletion fails, or otherwise verify that the output was replaced before reading it.

The deterministic mode sum differs from the reported GLM value by 0.0489 and is declared a match only because this line introduces an unexplained 0.05 cutoff. Since the audit explicitly did not run GLM's random-phase generator or structure-function estimator and provides no seed distribution or uncertainty for that difference, this establishes model-level consistency but cannot exclude an implementation error; reproduce the reviewed estimator or quantify the statistical and numerical errors before emitting `true` and concluding “NOT B.”

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierPhysics/blob/73584dc80ad7c3a079de3bd73163b172b301dd77/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)
